title: package wata-server so it runs consistently on the host mac: survives reboot and logout, restarts on failure, versioned data dir + log rotation, one command to install/uninstall
minimal Sgola port of the TS tui: a cheap second client and the admin interface (list rooms/users, send/play voice, poke the server) — reuses wataclient, terminal-only
wifi/cellular/reconnecting status in the wata UI proper (not just settings rows) — M4's UI-clarity condition; then the M4 flip test
settings subsumes the text menu entirely so system-menu can retire: audit what system-menu.py still offers beyond IP/cell/battery/power and fold in what earns its place
start wata-fb as early as init allows; UI presents a calm starting-up/waiting-for-network state over the existing backoff instead of an error surface
family (group) rooms as a first-class concept the way DMs are: server-owned membership, a create/join path a kid can use, and the client UI for it
boot logo end to end: aboot splash partition frame, kernel quiet/fbcon-logo suppression, hand-off to wata-fb's first frame

HELD (2026-08-05: no phone app yet) — device mints its own keypair; parent's phone scans a QR the device displays and approves it into the server allowlist. Unblock when there is a phone client to scan with.
openrc reports net-watchdog crashed while the process runs (lost pidfile) — no auto-restart and a lying status; fix supervision before relying on wifi/cellular failover
wifi configuration panel: scan/select/enter a network for a device that has no keyboard — driven from the tui over the client-server link, not typed on the handset
minimal phone client: scan an enrolment QR and approve it, plus a real second client — unblocks IROH-ONBOARD; design in plan 0008
favouriting a message exempts it from the retention sweep — the Retain.exemptEventIds seam exists and has no caller yet
an allowlist refusal (QUIC close 401 'not allowlisted') reads client-side as a generic closed connection; surface the reason so a human can tell 'not enrolled' from 'server down'
